messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: boost 1.60...
parts:
Hi!

upgrading boost is already long in the issue tracker. Any obvious reason no update has been made yet?

What are the requirements for acceptance when we upgrade boost? I mean, in this case to my knowledge things still work for Stan, but you end up getting some warning messages from the compiler due to some deprecated stuff. So is it required to address those deprecated messages right away when taking care of the upgrade. Or can we push these secondary issues into further issues?

The boost odeint solver has gotten a very important upgrade (implementation of max_num_step functionality) which I would like to enable ASAP.

Sebastian

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] boost 1.60...
parts:
> On Mar 16, 2016, at 6:24 AM, Sebastian Weber <sdw....@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi!
>
> upgrading boost is already long in the issue tracker. Any obvious reason no update has been made yet?
>
> What are the requirements for acceptance when we upgrade boost? I mean, in this case to my knowledge things still work for Stan, but you end up getting some warning messages from the compiler due to some deprecated stuff. So is it required to address those deprecated messages right away when taking care of the upgrade. Or can we push these secondary issues into further issues?

We move forward when the bh package in R (boost headers) move forward. For every interface other than R, we distribute boost.

It's a matter of practical integration issues. If we move forward with the boost version before bh, then it's very possible some part of Stan will be incompatible with one of our major interfaces.

This is the same reason we haven't gone to c++11.

>
> The boost odeint solver has gotten a very important upgrade (implementation of max_num_step functionality) which I would like to enable ASAP.

> Sebastian
